Key Takeaways

Cloudflare stock is down 11% in the past month. An AI and software selloff that also hit Datadog and CrowdStrike pulled it lower, even though Cloudflare just posted its fastest revenue growth in nearly four years.

Third-quarter revenue rose 39% to $782.5 million. Cloudflare raised its 2026 outlook and now expects a GAAP profit in the fourth quarter.

Gross margin keeps sliding as AI traffic raises the network bill, and CrowdStrike's deal for Zscaler would create a bigger rival to Cloudflare's higher-margin Zero Trust business.

At 21% below its high, Cloudflare looks worth buying in pieces, and the fourth-quarter report expected in February is the next test.

Cloudflare (NET:NYSE) just posted its fastest revenue growth in nearly four years, and its stock is still down1 11% in the past month.

Blame the AI trade. The same selloff hit Datadog (DDOG:NASDAQ) far harder. And on Nov. 23, CrowdStrike (CRWD:NASDAQ) agreed to buy Zscaler, one of Cloudflare's zero-trust rivals.

The AI selloff dragged it down twice

Cloudflare had no news of its own when ServiceNow's and Fortinet's Oct. 28 reports revived fears that AI is disrupting software. Datadog's outlook on Nov. 4 and the Democratic sweep of Congress the next day spread the AI selloff to cloud software. The selloff deepened again on Nov. 20 as Anthropic fell on its second trading day. The Nasdaq 100 fell 8% in the month.

Datadog makes the sharpest contrast. Both companies grew revenue 36% in the second quarter. Then Datadog guided fourth-quarter revenue to $1.19 billion to $1.20 billion, flat with its third quarter. A day later, Cloudflare guided to 8% growth over its third quarter. Datadog is down 37% in the month.

Its best quarter in nearly four years kept it afloat

On Nov. 5, Cloudflare reported third-quarter revenue of $782.5 million, up 39% and above the $739.7 million analysts expected. It guided fourth-quarter revenue to $845 million to $846 million, against $798.2 million expected. It also raised its 2026 outlook to about $2.96 billion. Management now expects a GAAP profit in the fourth quarter, well ahead of its 2028 target.

"Our engine is firing on all cylinders, and we've found an even higher gear for this next phase of growth," CEO Matthew Prince said.
